Replay

Typed scene adapters

4 min readOdin × GodotPage source ↓
On this page ↓
Script descriptorsIteration and scopeDiagnostics and data ownershipOptional generationAuthoring previews

The adapter chooses presentation data and game lifetime boundaries. Shared owners handle script resolution, borrowed pointers, asset retention, callback configuration, entity membership and diagnostics. Scrapyard uses the same binding declarations for authored enemy scenes and permanent runner scenes.

Script descriptors#

Script_View(Value, Script) has one optional validate callback returning a definitions.Report identifying the exact failed component. The display type must be a bounded replayable value. Script pointers, local clocks and Godot objects belong to the view script, not its display value.

Odin
descriptor := scenegd.Script_View(Runner_Display, Runner_View){
    present  = runner_present,
    validate = runner_validate,
}

When migrating an older descriptor, replace valid = check with validate = validate_view. Return {} on success or definitions.problem(.Invalid, field, message) on failure; retain every check from the old predicate. valid is no longer a descriptor field and old initializers fail compilation. In an archetype binding, validation checks scene components before configure supplies the appearance. A directly bound scene that requires an authored appearance must validate that appearance as well.

Script_Binding(Value, Script) stores that descriptor by value and borrows a permanent authored node. script_bind resolves and validates its script; script_present passes a detached value; script_release invokes optional retirement and releases the binding, without freeing the node. Release before the node is freed or rebound. It never decides that a body generation, warp or epoch change should replace a permanent scene. Scrapyard's runner retains its node and handles those display transitions explicitly in its script.

For entity scenes with authored appearances:

Odin
descriptor := scenegd.Script_Archetype(Enemy_Display, Enemy_View, Enemy_Style){
    view = {
        present  = enemy_present,
        validate = enemy_validate,
        retired  = enemy_retire,
    },
    configure = enemy_configure, // proc(^Enemy_View, ^Enemy_Style)->defs.Report
}
views: scenegd.Script_Archetypes(Enemy, Enemy_Display, Enemy_View, Enemy_Style)
report := scenegd.script_archetypes_init(&views, &assets, parent, CAPACITY,
    select_kind, descriptor)

This owner copies configuration, allocates stable callback contexts, and retains appearance resources. Underlying view pools retain their scenes. The source registry can close after successful initialization. Keep the owner at a stable address and destroy it before its parent/script module disappears. It resolves the root script after _ready, validates scene components, resolves the exact appearance script, then calls configure. Configure validates/applies appearance; scene validation should not require appearance configuration to have happened yet.

script_archetypes_present returns an owned diagnostic on failure. retired must accept partial initialization and end all borrowed-resource use; queued node removal completes later. Ordinary process callbacks should stop after retirement. Nodes/scripts remain Godot-owned. No callback may reenter or mutate membership of its view owner.

Iteration and scope#

view_pool_visit, archetype_pool_visit and script_archetypes_visit provide typed entity handles and rigs/scripts to a callback with a typed user pointer. Use them to drain local visual notices without depending on bucket/index storage. Borrowed storage must not escape the visit. Matching *_stats functions provide aggregate node/paint/property counters.

view.Scope_Tracker(Key) compares explicit inputs:

Odin
scope, error := view.scope_update(&tracker,
    {epoch, reset_serial, observed_tick},
    World_View_Key{run, floor},
    rewind_resets = true)

The caller chooses the key and whether backwards observation time resets a view lifetime. Forward ticks and unchanged keys preserve scope; epoch/reset/key changes advance the revision. Zero/stale epochs, unsupported key types and revision exhaustion fail without changing the tracker. It does not infer authority, sample prediction, use correction counts as reset events, or know what a floor means.

Diagnostics and data ownership#

view_pool_problem and archetype_pool_problem retain detailed diagnostics while existing low-level presentation functions still return their original error enum. Script-based owners return the diagnostic directly. Errors identify archetype, scene path, entity key and the component/field supplied by the typed validator. Input validation precedes membership changes; arbitrary scene _ready code and instantiation side effects do not become transactional.

Resource_Batch loads a bounded directory of .tres/.res resources, retaining the whole candidate set until resource_batch_destroy. Loading failure publishes no partial batch. It rejects reinitializing a live batch, preserving the existing one. Use resource_script(resource, Script, path) for checked borrowed script access, or bake_resource(ctx, resource, Script, path) inside an extractor.

bake_integer(ctx, u16, source, minimum, maximum, path) checks explicit domain and representation bounds before narrowing. Supported targets are fixed 8/16/32-bit signed/unsigned integers. Inspector ranges are editing hints, not inferred game validation. Complex mappings, nested dependencies and cross-field rules remain explicit functions. Scrapyard shares one defs.bake_mob among live admission, artifact export and previews; no second generated extractor is introduced.

Optional generation#

Place this declaration above the script's package line:

Odin
//gd:replay_view value=value,present=enemy_present,validate=enemy_validate,retired=enemy_retire,appearance=skin,configure=enemy_configure

value names a direct display field; appearance names a direct typed Resource script pointer. present is required, validate and retired are optional; appearance and configure must appear together. Procedures are ordinary same-package Odin procedures. The script must extend Node2D or a compatible class.

The generated <snake_script_name>_replay_binding() returns Script_View or Script_Archetype, with compile-time assertions on callback signatures. Types come from the named fields, so imported display types need no duplicate import/mapping in generated code. Unknown/duplicate options and missing fields fail generation. It emits no simulation state, wire registration, sampling policy, signals or extra lifecycle callbacks. Unannotated scripts keep their existing generation behavior.

Handwritten descriptors use exactly the same public helpers. Actual scene nodes, Resource scripts and required components are validated in Godot; code generation alone cannot prove that every PackedScene has the expected hierarchy.

Authoring previews#

Use existing typed onready fields for composed scripts:

Odin
charge: ^ScrapChargeView `gd:"onready=Charge"`,

Scrapyard's ScrapEnemyPreview Resource references a MobDef and supplies sample attack/warning/charge state. The same mob extractor validates the definition, and a detached display is baked on scene startup. A pulse radius comes from the selected definition; there is no switch over known enemy IDs. The authoring tools provide explicit refresh of isolated preview data; live-bound views reject refresh. Appearance and normal scene-local animations remain independent of Session/World, with the same display interface as live play.
